summary: A 2019 survey of the uprisings then under way in Hong Kong, Catalonia, Chile, Lebanon, Egypt and Iraq, and of Turkey's assault on Rojava, focusing on state violence against protesters and how movements learned from each other.

evidence.note: host frames it as an unusual episode on uprisings happening now, with activists as the only guests
Catalonia segment begins, running to the 2019 sentencing of separatist leaders
2017 independence referendum and crackdown, the earliest event covered at length
Rojava segment: Turkish attack of October 2019 and refugee crisis via a local reporter
Trump abandons the SDF to Erdogan; China backs Madrid, autocrats supporting each other
Chilean inequality, privatisation and Gini coefficient discussed at length
several minutes on conspiracy theories about bus and power-company arson in Santiago
martial law in Chile, soldiers beating and shooting protesters
Lebanon segment: wildfires, WhatsApp tax, mass protests and reforms
Egypt segment: Sisi crushes the September 2019 protests, internet blocked
Iraqi protesters killed by tear gas canisters fired into their heads, described vividly

notes: Subject cap of five: Hong Kong protests are the thread running through the episode but get only a short segment of their own, so they appear in setting and keywords, not as a subject. Iraq gets about two minutes and is left out of setting. Catalan history from the 1920s and the Syrian civil war are background, so covered_span starts at the 2017 referendum.
